synopsis: Southwest Research Institute (SwRI) is identified as a research organization with current off-road or heavy-machinery relevance, offering off-road software-in-the-loop scene and camera-vision autonomy tools for military, space and agriculture applications [f8665, f8833, f16080]. Its cited tool evidence is labeled vendor evidence and concerns off-road applications, not construction or mining [f8696, f8834]. Separately, its 2024 study provides independent evidence by comparing photogrammetric replicas of unstructured outdoor environments with real imagery using image entropy and structural texture similarity, which agreed well [f4756, f4757, f4759]. Those metrics also correlated with visual-odometry behaviour as simulated gamma varied, extending the assessment beyond visual appearance to application behaviour [f4758, f4828]. This supports texture and gamma validation in off-road-like natural environments, but does not validate severe weather, glare, mud or night radiometry [f4759].
